question.problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $(x+5)^{2}=-20(y+2)?$
question.worked_solution:
The standard equation of an upward- or downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ is

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

where $p$ is constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)^{2} & =4(-5)(y+2).\end{aligned}
$$

It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with $p=-5.$

Comparing our equation with the standard equation, we can see that we have $h=-5$ and $k=-2.$ Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola are $(-5,-2).$
